text:
anya: quick architecture question- we're adding multi-model routing with fallbacks (fast-small -> high-quality-large). need a solid accounting model so billing and perf dashboards match reality. current tracing only marks top-level request.

ben: are we charging per-invocation or per-token? multi-model complicates both. if small model responds normally and large model is only used on failure, cost attribution must split.

rachel: ops constraint: billing pipeline expects one canonical set of attributes per request for join keys. I'd rather we emit a compact cost-span that summarizes model usage per request.

omar: sketch idea: add a cost_span object attached to the root trace with these fields: request_id, models_used = [(model_id, tokens_in, peak_gpu_ms)], total_cost_estimate, decision_path. Keep it compact to avoid trace bloat.

kevin: can't have nested objects in the trace payload today. prefer a flat encoded header: COST-SPAN=v1;rid=...;m1=mistral-7b:tokens=24:gpu=12ms; m2=redwood-xl:tokens=128:gpu=134ms;cost_cents=3.45

anya: that flat header looks fine for collectors to parse. two questions: 1) who composes it (edge SDK vs runtime) and 2) how do we handle retries and dedupe so we don't double-bill?

ben: compose at the runtime layer (router) because it sees the whole decision path. SDK would have to trace internals which is messy. runtime emits COST-SPAN on the root span before sending response.

rachel: dedupe: require a stable request_id (X-Req-Fingerprint) generated at edge. billing dedup logic: if same request_id within 60s, collapse by taking max(cost) or prefer final completed span. we should capture attempt_index too.

omar: about sampling: if request sampling drops the root, we'd lose cost spans. we should make COST-SPAN high-priority — always emit to billing index even for sampled traces. That requires separate light-weight path off the router to the billing sink.

kevin: tradeoff: end-to-end latency vs write amplification. alternative: emit cost-span asynchronously to a dedicated UDP/HTTP fire-and-forget endpoint with strict rate-limiting. cheap and non-blocking.

anya: sounds reasonable. compliance check: any cost-span that contains tenant identifiers must obey allowlist and not include PII. rachel, we need to ensure the billing sink has restricted access.

rachel: noted. also add expiration to cost-span records (retain 90 days), and store an integrity hash (sha256) of the serialized span for audit.

ben: operational note: we'll need to update downstream dashboards to calculate per-model unit cost. propose we standardize units: tokens_in (int), gpu_ms (int), model_version (string), and cost_cents (int cents). Avoid floats for cents.

omar: propose header format RFC in repo and sample parser pseudocode. I'll draft mapping and parser in Go. key points: stable delim, urlsafe base64 for decision_path if it gets long.

kevin: rollout plan idea:
- phase 0: runtime emits COST-SPAN to log only (no billing join) for 72h
- phase 1: billing pipeline ingests cost-spans in dry-run and compares with invoice model
- phase 2: enable attribution merges with dedupe rules

anya: action items:
- omar: RFC + example parser + tests by next Wed
- ben: update billing join keys + dedupe algo prototype by next Tue
- rachel: ACL & retention policy + secure sink checklist by next Mon
- kevin: a tiny non-blocking emitter lib (node/go) for runtimes by EOD Fri

ops-bot: created task: infra/emit-cost-span -> canary pipeline pending. monitor: billing-match-rate and cost-delta metric.

anya: thanks team. if anyone has concerns about per-token vs per-invocation accounting tradeoffs, flag them here. Otherwise I'll put RFC draft in PR and add examples for router + fallback flows. :thumbsup:
